name: Kāna and its sisters
definition: Verbs that come upon a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, keep the first in rafʿ as their ism, and put the second in naṣb as their khabar.
body: Kāna 'was' and its sisters do not tell of an act but of time or a state: they add it to a nominal sentence. Their ism stays marfūʿ and their khabar becomes manṣūb: zaydun qāʾimun becomes kāna zaydun qāʾiman.
Al-Ājurrūmiyya lists them: kāna, amsā, aṣbaḥa, aḍḥā, ẓalla, bāta, ṣāra, laysa, mā zāla, mā nfakka, mā fatiʾa, mā bariḥa, mā dāma, and what is formed from them (yakūnu, kun, yuṣbiḥu …).

examples.text: Zayd was standing: zaydun the ism of kāna, qāʾiman its khabar.
